question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\left(8 - 4 x\right) e^{- y - 3}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\left(8 - 4 x\right) e^{- y - 3} \\ (e^{y + 3})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =8 - 4 x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (e^{y + 3})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (8 - 4 x)\,\text{d}x \\ \int (e^{y + 3})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int (8 - 4 x)\,\text{d}x \\ \int (e^{y + 3})\,\text{d}y & =\int (8 - 4 x)\,\text{d}x \\ e^{y + 3} & =- 2 \left(x - 2\right)^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
e^{y + 3}=- 2 \left(x - 2\right)^{2}+C.
$$

$$
